content:
I've noticed that the time it takes to spawn a process can be significantly impacted by the size of the environment.

-- No Mathlib import

open IO in
def timeSpawnWithout : IO Unit := do
  let n := 20
  let start ← monoMsNow
  for _ in [0:n] do
    let child ← Process.spawn { cmd := "/bin/echo", args := #["hi"], stdout := .piped, stderr := .piped, stdin := .piped }
    let _ ← child.wait
  let elapsed := (← monoMsNow) - start
  IO.println s!"WITHOUT Mathlib: {n} spawns took {elapsed}ms ({elapsed.toFloat / n.toFloat}ms each)"

#eval timeSpawnWithout

If I run the above code snippet on v4.30.0, I get the output WITHOUT Mathlib: 20 spawns took 391ms (19.550000ms each). If I run the analogous code snippet timeSpawnWith (which is identical except that line 1 is replaced with import Mathlib), I get the output WITH Mathlib: 20 spawns took 51849ms (2592.450000ms each). I've observed this behavior on Mac and Windows, but not on Linux. On Linux, there is still a bump, but it is much smaller, (e.g. 118ms (5.900000ms each) ↦ 1411ms (70.550000ms each)).

  • Is this a known issue?
  • If so, is there a known workaround (besides asking people to keep their imports minimal)?

Hey Josh, that's certainly an interesting observation. It looks like on macOS we could optimize the implementation to avoid that but I have no clue about Windows. Any chance a virus scanner or similar is involved there?

It's totally possible that a virus scanner or some other third variable is confounding the measurement on Windows. I'm primarily a Mac user and am just borrowing a Windows laptop for some tests, so it's very plausible that I don't have things set up 100% correctly on the Windows machine. I'll try to look into it and confirm one way or the other if that's the issue.

I'm much more confident that I have things set up correctly on Mac though.

Update: Yep, on Windows it was a virus scanner problem, and resolving that issue made Windows behave more like Linux. I'm still reasonably confident I have things set up correctly on Mac, but if someone would be able to confirm they're able to replicate this behavior, that would help give me peace of mind.
Yes, that entirely fixes the discrepancy on my end. Thanks!
Just wanted to follow up on this: Are there any known plans to have this PR merged? If not, are there other workarounds I should explore?
Aha, I think this might explain some behavior I was running into as well. :)
